stem: Which statement best describes the role of the European alliance system in the outbreak of World War I?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The alliances were created by the League of Nations to keep the peace, and they prevented each government from mobilizing.
choices.explanation: The League of Nations was created after the war.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The alliances prevented conflict by making every state friendly with every other, so no government had reason to arm or mobilize.
choices.explanation: The system divided Europe into opposing blocs and increased the chance that a local crisis would spread.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Germany and France were allies against Russia from the beginning of the crisis, and Britain stayed neutral until the war ended in 1918.
choices.explanation: Germany and France were on opposite sides.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rival alliances committed the major powers to support their partners, so a regional crisis after the Sarajevo assassination grew into a general war.
choices.explanation: Austria-Hungary's conflict with Serbia drew in Russia, Germany, France and Britain through alliance obligations and mobilization plans.

explanation: Rival alliances turned a regional conflict into a world war.

stem:
> “We have been under shell fire for six days. The dead lie in the wire between the lines, and after all the attacks the front has moved only a few hundred yards. They tell us the next push will break through.”
>
> *Source: A soldier's letter from the Western Front, 1916*

Which statement best explains the situation described in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neither army had artillery, so both relied on rifles alone and on massed infantry charges across open fields.
choices.explanation: Artillery was extensively used on the Western Front.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Machine guns, barbed wire and artillery favored defenders, so frontal assaults were extremely costly and produced trench warfare.
choices.explanation: New weapons favored defense, and neither side could achieve a breakthrough without heavy casualties.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The war was ended by an armistice that was in effect in 1916, and soldiers stayed in the trenches as guards.
choices.explanation: The armistice came in November 1918.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cavalry charges had proven to be the decisive weapon for attackers, and the generals relied on them to break the line.
choices.explanation: Cavalry was largely ineffective against machine guns and artillery.

explanation: Defensive technology produced a deadlock and heavy casualties.

stem:
> “Peace, land and bread.”
>
> *Source: A slogan used by the Bolsheviks in Russia, 1917*

Which factor best explains the appeal of the slogan to many Russians in 1917?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Widespread discontent with the costly war, shortages of food, and peasants' hunger for land under the Provisional Government.
choices.explanation: The slogan addressed the main grievances of soldiers, workers and peasants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A desire to continue the war with greater effort until the Central Powers were defeated, which most soldiers and workers wanted by 1917.
choices.explanation: The slogan called for peace.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Support for the restoration of the tsar, whom many Russians hoped would return from exile.
choices.explanation: The slogan promised change after the tsar's fall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gratitude for German help with the harvest, which had been organized by a treaty with the Provisional Government.
choices.explanation: Germany was an enemy and had not helped the harvest.

explanation: The slogan responded to war weariness, hunger and land hunger.

stem: Which statement best describes the effect of World War I on the home fronts of the combatant nations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Governments reduced their control over the economy in order to promote free enterprise, and ended rationing, censorship and military conscription for the duration of the war.
choices.explanation: Governments expanded control during the war.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Civilians were separated from the war and their daily lives were unchanged by the fighting abroad.
choices.explanation: Civilians were deeply affected by shortages, labor demands and sometimes direct attack.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Industries shut down because they were not needed for the war, and most workers were sent home.
choices.explanation: Industries expanded to produce war materials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Governments mobilized economies and populations through rationing, controlling industry and propaganda, and women took jobs in factories.
choices.explanation: Total war involved the whole society and increased the power of the state.

explanation: Total war increased state control and changed work for women.

stem:
> “The Allied governments affirm, and Germany accepts, that Germany and her allies are responsible for causing all the loss and damage suffered by the Allied governments and their peoples as a result of the war imposed upon them.”
>
> *Source: A summary of a clause of the Treaty of Versailles, 1919*

Which development was most directly connected to the clause described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Widespread German resentment over blame and reparations, which later nationalist and Nazi propaganda exploited.
choices.explanation: Many Germans considered the treaty humiliating, and extremist movements used that resentment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The immediate entry of the United States into the League of Nations as a founding member, which strengthened the treaty.
choices.explanation: The United States Senate refused to ratify the treaty and did not join the League.

choices.label: C
choices.text: German gratitude toward the Allies for the generous terms of the settlement.
choices.explanation: Many Germans felt the terms were harsh and unfair.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The restoration of the German monarchy under the Kaiser's grandson.
choices.explanation: The German monarchy had fallen at the end of the war.

explanation: The war guilt clause and reparations fueled German resentment.

stem: Which factor best explains why the Great Depression that began in 1929 spread around the world?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interconnected economies, with international trade, loans and investment, meant the collapse of the American economy and credit spread to other countries.
choices.explanation: The financial and trade links among industrial economies carried the crisis across borders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1929, which disrupted trade with every European power.
choices.explanation: The Soviet Union existed until 1991.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the United States was affected by the crash, because other economies were isolated from American banks, trade and lending and kept their own currencies.
choices.explanation: Many countries suffered high unemployment and falling trade.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A sudden discovery of new gold supplies raised prices everywhere and led to a wave of speculation.
choices.explanation: The Depression was marked by falling prices and production.

explanation: Links among national economies carried the crisis worldwide.

stem: Which statement best explains the appeal of fascist movements in Italy and Germany in the 1920s and 1930s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They offered a democratic socialist program based on international cooperation, free elections, and the protection of minority rights in every country.
choices.explanation: Fascists rejected democracy and internationalism.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They opposed all forms of nationalism and wanted to dissolve the existing states of Europe.
choices.explanation: Nationalism was central to fascism.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They promised national revival, order and recovery in societies shaken by defeat, depression and fear of communism, and they used propaganda and violence.
choices.explanation: Fascists appealed to nationalism and to people seeking strong leadership in a period of crisis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They advocated that the League of Nations should govern the world through a single international army.
choices.explanation: Fascist regimes opposed and ignored the League.

explanation: Fascism combined extreme nationalism, authoritarian leadership and promises of recovery.

stem: Stalin's policies of collectivization and the Five-Year Plans in the Soviet Union aimed primarily to

choices.label: A
choices.text: focus the economy on consumer goods rather than heavy industry, so that workers could buy more clothing, food and household goods.
choices.explanation: The Five-Year Plans emphasized heavy industry and military goods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: rapidly industrialize the country and put agriculture under state control, at enormous human cost.
choices.explanation: The policies sought to build heavy industry and control food production, and they caused famine and repression.

choices.label: C
choices.text: reduce state control and encourage small business and foreign investment in the villages.
choices.explanation: State control increased.

choices.label: D
choices.text: restore private farms and a market economy to feed the cities.
choices.explanation: The policies abolished private farms and market incentives.

explanation: Stalin's plans were meant to industrialize rapidly under state control.

stem:
> “We shall march to the sea and take salt from its shores in defiance of the law that forbids it. We shall use no violence, but we shall refuse to obey a law that is unjust.”
>
> *Source: Statement by an Indian nationalist leader announcing a protest, 1930*

Which statement best describes the strategy of the movement described in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It used nonviolent civil disobedience to challenge British authority and win popular support.
choices.explanation: Gandhi's Salt March was a nonviolent act of civil disobedience that mobilized Indians across social groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It was an armed insurrection against the British army, aimed at seizing the arsenals of the empire.
choices.explanation: The passage rejects violence.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It was an alliance with Japan against the British, signed before the outbreak of the war.
choices.explanation: The passage does not mention any alliance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It was a campaign to encourage emigration from India to colonies elsewhere in the British Empire.
choices.explanation: The passage concerns protest within India.

explanation: The passage describes nonviolent civil disobedience.

stem: Which statement best describes the policy of appeasement toward Nazi Germany in the 1930s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Britain and France formed a military alliance with the Soviet Union to invade Germany immediately after the Anschluss, forcing Hitler to retreat.
choices.explanation: They avoided military confrontation until Germany invaded Poland in 1939.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Britain and France openly supported Germany's war against Poland and sent it arms and supplies.
choices.explanation: Britain and France declared war on Germany after the invasion of Poland.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Britain and France enforced strict military sanctions through the League of Nations, which halted every German advance.
choices.explanation: The League's sanctions were weak and appeasement involved concessions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Britain and France made concessions to Hitler, such as accepting the German takeover of the Sudetenland at Munich in 1938, hoping to avoid war.
choices.explanation: Appeasement was an attempt to satisfy Hitler's demands to preserve peace, and it was not successful.

explanation: Appeasement meant making concessions to avoid war.

stem: Which statement best explains Japan's expansion in East Asia in the 1930s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Japan was a member of the Allies and was defending its Pacific territories against a German invasion fleet.
choices.explanation: Japan joined the Axis powers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Japan was a colony of a European power and was seeking independence by attacking its mainland neighbors.
choices.explanation: Japan was an independent imperial power.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Japan was fulfilling an obligation to the League of Nations to protect China from warlords, and withdrew its forces from Manchuria as soon as order was restored.
choices.explanation: The League criticized Japan's actions in Manchuria, and Japan left the League.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Japanese leaders, increasingly influenced by the military, sought raw materials, markets and regional dominance, invading Manchuria in 1931 and China in 1937.
choices.explanation: Japan's expansion was driven by resource needs, nationalism and militarist influence.

explanation: Japan's expansion was motivated by resources, nationalism and militarism.

stem: Which statement best describes how the Holocaust differed from earlier episodes of religious or ethnic persecution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It was carried out by the Soviet Union against its own population during the 1930s.
choices.explanation: The Holocaust was carried out by Nazi Germany and its collaborators.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It was directed only against soldiers in wartime, and followed the rules of war on prisoners.
choices.explanation: The victims were mostly civilians.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It used the state's bureaucracy, modern technology and a racial ideology to carry out systematic mass murder.
choices.explanation: The Nazi regime organized the identification, transport and killing of about six million Jews, along with millions of other victims, through state institutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It was a spontaneous series of riots without any government involvement, led by local mobs in a handful of towns and ending within a few weeks.
choices.explanation: The persecution was planned and carried out by the state.

explanation: The Holocaust was an organized, state-run genocide using modern bureaucracy and technology.

stem: The use of atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945 most directly contributed to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The end of the war in Europe, which had already ended in May of that year.
choices.explanation: The war in Europe had ended in May 1945.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Japan's surrender, which ended World War II, and the beginning of the nuclear age and the arms race.
choices.explanation: The bombings were followed by Japan's surrender and shaped later rivalry between the superpowers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The beginning of World War II, in the same year as the invasion of Poland.
choices.explanation: The war began in 1939.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The immediate surrender of the Soviet Union, which had been fighting Japan in Manchuria and Korea since August.
choices.explanation: The Soviet Union was an Allied power.

explanation: The bombs were followed by Japan's surrender and ushered in the nuclear age.

stem: The Armenian Genocide of 1915 is best understood as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Russian campaign against the Ottoman people, carried out by the Tsar's armies on the Caucasus front.
choices.explanation: It was carried out by the Ottoman government against Armenians.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A battle between the Ottoman and Russian armies, fought on the Caucasus front during the winter of 1915.
choices.explanation: The genocide targeted a civilian population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A peaceful population exchange agreed by the Ottoman and Armenian leaders, with compensation for lost property and safe passage for all.
choices.explanation: It was a campaign of forced deportation and killing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The deportation and mass killing of Armenians by the Ottoman government during World War I, linked to nationalism and wartime fears.
choices.explanation: Ottoman authorities deported and killed large numbers of Armenians in 1915 and afterwards.

explanation: The Armenian Genocide was a government-led campaign of deportation and killing during World War I.

stem: The mandate system created after World War I is best described as

choices.label: A
choices.text: a system in which the United States governed the former German colonies in Africa as mandates, under a charter from the Senate that lasted until the end of the Second World War.
choices.explanation: The mandatory powers were mainly Britain, France and Japan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: a plan for the former colonies to rejoin the German Empire, with the consent of the League of Nations.
choices.explanation: Germany lost its colonies in the peace settlement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: an immediate grant of independence to all former colonies of the defeated powers, with free elections held under League supervision in every territory.
choices.explanation: Most mandated territories were not independent, and nationalists continued their struggle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the League of Nations' assignment of former Ottoman and German territories to Britain, France and other powers, which governed them as mandates while nationalists sought independence.
choices.explanation: The mandates were a new form of imperial control, justified as preparation for self-government.

explanation: Mandates transferred defeated powers' territories to the victors under League authority.
